_help.about: Walls of fitted stone for Torchfire 1's ruins: the Inca way, every stone its own polygon, fitted with no mortar; real relief, never a normal map; settled with age; overgrown only where it would really grow. First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; Claude Code matches the shape to its generator (keep the meaning, rename freely) and Mike tunes by playing. Built 6 Oct by Claude Code (FittedStone, TombBuild): every seen tomb wall face. Restart after editing.
_help.partition: How a wall face is cut into stones. method: voronoi (one cell per stone on the wall plane). seed_per_face: every wall face takes its own seed, so joints never mirror across a corridor (Mike's 6 Oct note). relax_steps: smoothing passes so cells are rounder and more even (0 = raw, more = more regular). corner_rule: stones at a wall's corner wrap or stop at the edge (stop is the first guess; wrap if the corners look cut). Built: the cells are laid in loose courses (presets course_bias), then relaxed relax_steps times (each site moved to its cell's middle, Lloyd's way).
_help.relief: Real geometry (R-rules: no normal maps, no shine). proud_m: how far a stone's face stands out from the wall plane [min, max]. pillow_m: how much its face bulges in the middle. bevel_m: the rounded edge's width. joint_m: the gap left between stones at the face. joint_depth_m: how deep the joints sink. joint_occlusion: baked occlusion in the joints, tinted to the scene's shade colour (navy, olive in green scenes, never grey; §ES.2). The torch's live light catches the pillowed faces. Built: each stone's proud is rolled in proud_m; joint_occlusion scene_shade darkens the joints and the stones' feet toward the scene's shade (Prelit.ao_tint: navy, olive on green); a preset's own relief block overrides these for its stones.
_help.settle: Fitted but settled (§EU.3): share of stones that have moved; offset_m: in (negative) or out (positive) [min, max]; tilt_deg [min, max]; dropped_share: stones fallen out of their place (rare; a collapsed room, crawler.json kit.kinds collapsed, is where the rubble lives). Built: tilt turns the stone in the wall's plane; a dropped stone sinks dropped_m and tilts double.
_help.overgrowth: §EU.4: only where it would really grow. climate: the moisture and temperature gate is vines.json climate (moisture[0] none, moisture[1] full, fades outside temp_c, shade_boost). moss_in_joints: moss gathers in the recessed joints first. moss_low_wall_m: moss climbs the shaded lower wall to this height at full climate. vines: vines from cracks and wall tops, the biome's own vine species, drawn per vines.json. dry: where the climate gives no moss, sand and dust drift into corners (drift_corner_m deep). Built (Claude Code): the place's climate is its world's biome (worlds.json worlds[*].theme -> biome -> data/biomes climate, the middle of its moisture and temp_c ranges); a theme with no world yet uses stand_in (the tomb, until §EW places it: open for Mike). Underground is all shade (shade 1 in the joints and low on the wall, half-shade higher up). density scales it all; joint_moss and low_moss how green the joints and the lower wall go at full climate; wet: how the moisture wanders inside a place (vary, over scale_m) and rises each flight down (per_flight), so areas differ on their own; vines_per_m and vine_len_m the vines (generic ivy until a world has a biome with vine species); dry: where the climate gives no moss, drifts_per_m drifts a metre of wall foot, drift_h_m high, reaching drift_corner_m out (deeper in the corners), color.
_help.presets: §EU.5. stone_m: a stone's typical width [min, max]; course_bias: 0 = free polygons, 1 = loosely in courses (rows); tint: the stone's colour (sRGB hex) or "theme" for the stage's existing stone colour. megalithic: a few huge stones (Sacsayhuamán). fitted_small: many tight stones. Built: aspect is a stone's width over its height (Inca courses run wide); a preset's relief block overrides relief for it (small stones want a smaller bevel and pillow). With a style (§EX.1), the style's stone.tint and spread colour every stone and a preset's tint is not read.
_help.by_theme: Which preset each crawler.json theme uses (first guess, open for Mike, §EU). Per world with §EW (worlds.json). A theme not listed takes default.
_help.seed: Claude Code: 0 takes the stones from the tomb's own seed (each tomb its own stones; every wall face then hashes its own seed from it, partition.seed_per_face); any other number pins the layout.
_help.styles: A ruin type's whole kit (Mike, 6 Oct: "each ruins type has a homogenized and thoughtful layout and aesthetic … crafted out of the same materials"). Every built stone surface in a ruin draws from its style: rule.every_surface. One stone: stone.tint ("theme" as the presets) with stone.spread, the most any one stone strays from it (lighter or darker); rule.no_general_palette: nothing built of stone takes RuinBuilder's general palette or a hard-coded colour (the floor flags, the ceiling slabs, the stairs and the sconces did, 37fd8a7). rule.on_top: what may lie over the stone without being a second stone (the heart's ochre is paint, §BQ; soot §EV.1; moss and drift §EU.4). module_m: the builders' unit; room sides, corridor lengths and the spacing of doors and sconces are whole numbers of it (§EX.2). heights_m: the short list of ceiling heights (the kit's own as built). walls.preset: a presets entry. floor: method fitted_flags (the walls' Voronoi cutter laid flat, stones stone_scale times the wall's, pillow and proud times pillow_scale, joints packed with grit to joint_fill of their depth; wear: smoother and flatter along the middle of a passage, amount 0-1) or rough_slabs (big flags, the gaps packed with small stones, gap_share of the floor). ceiling: method lintel_slabs (single slabs wall to wall, slab_w_m wide each, settled like the walls) or corbel_vault (courses stepping in course_step_m each until a capstone closes it); rooms: how a room's ceiling starts (corbel_courses courses stepping corbel_step_m in, then the method); passages: a corridor's roof; gaps_share: passage capstones with a gap between them where snow and draft come in. max_span_m: no slab or vault spans wider; a wider room gets pillars of the style's stone on the module carrying stone beams, the ceiling spanning beam to beam. hearth_room four_pillars: four pillars round the hearth, the hearth's shaft (§EV.1) open between them (a megaron's plan). doors: shape trapezoid (top_share: the top's width over the foot's, the Inca batter) or trilithon (two uprights and a lintel); lintel monolith: one stone; threshold: one stone or a kerb stone. niches: the catacomb's bone shelves and any wall recess take this shape. stairs: block_steps (each step one block, settled like the walls) or big_blocks (few, broad). sconce: niche_cup (a niche of niches.shape cut in the wall, a stone cup in it, niche_w_m x niche_h_m) or recess_shelf (a recess between two orthostats, a flat stone shelf). dressing: coffins, benches, shelves and rubble of stone are cut from the style's stone. plan: how a ruin of this style lays out (§EX.2, crawler.json plan). models: the real places each is drawn from, for whoever builds it. First guesses by Claude (chat), 6 Oct; Mike tunes by playing (§EX.9 call 1). module_m and heights_m are read since 7 Oct (queue 46, §EX.2: TombKit lays the tomb's sizes in whole modules and its ceilings from heights_m); module_m also spaces the room sconces (§EX.4, queue 47) and the pillars (queue 48). Built 7 Oct (Claude Code, §EX.1, §EX.3; RuinStyle, TombBuild, FittedStone), for andean_tomb (the tomb); passage_grave_snow is data for when the snow ruins are built. One stone: every stone's colour is stone.tint ("theme": crawler.json themes.<theme>.stone; the tomb's is #636870, the mean its fitted walls showed before §EX, so the walls keep their tone) moved lighter or darker by up to stone.spread, every channel alike; the joints, feet and undersides go toward the scene's shade (navy) as the walls' do; RuinBuilder's palette is never read (TombBuild sets it to the style's own five tones, and the checks poison it). The walls' geometry is as before for the same seed: only the colour changed. floor: fitted_flags as above (FittedStone.flags); wear.band: how far out from a passage's middle the wear reaches (a share of its half width); wear.lighten: how far a fully worn flag goes toward the light end of the spread (0-1); in rooms the wear runs along the ways from each door to what the room holds (the hearth, the dead at the heart's end, else its middle). The flags' faces are one fan to the middle (no pillow ring: at pillow_scale it doesn't show), the collision one flat slab. ceiling: lintel_slabs, each slab a fitted stone drawn facing down (FittedStone.slabs), the joints between slabs a little out of true; rooms.corbel_h_m: the corbel course's height (corbel_step_m how far it steps in); the slabs span the room's shorter way. max_span_m and hearth_room four_pillars: where a room's span past its corbels is over max_span_m (and in the hearth room always), four pillars stand pillars.bays_modules modules apart round the room's middle (round the hearth), the first count that keeps every slab and beam span within max_span_m, a passage (0.9 m) clear of the walls, and the doors' ways in, the hearth, the mat, the bundle, the rescuer, a fire on the floor, the heart's box, the wall torches' bays (§EX.4), a crypt's coffin rows and the vents' columns clear (a single module, the 1 in bays_modules, only where no wider spacing stands clear; where none does, the spacing that crowds least, a torch's bay counting three times a coffin; a coffin a pillar stands on isn't laid, and no skeleton rests where it would climb out into one); two beams over them run wall to wall. pillars.side_m: a pillar's side (a base and a cap a little wider, drums between, settled a little); beam_w_m, beam_h_m: a beam's width and depth. The dressing keeps clear of the pillars. doors: trapezoid as above; jamb_w_m: the jamb stones' width up each side (three stacked, the doorway's shade in their faces); lintel_h_m: the monolithic lintel's height (it meets a room's corbel course when less than a course of wall would be left between them); bearing_m: how far the lintel reaches past the jambs. The threshold is one stone across the opening through the wall. niches: top_share for every niche; bone: the catacomb's bone niches (w_m wide at the foot, h_m high, depth_m deep, one at each of sills_m over the floor, a column every 1.4 m down both long walls clear of the doors and airways), the dead's bones and a skull on their sills; burial (Claude Code, 7 Oct, with queue 58's residents): where a skeleton sits, one tall niche in place of a column's two, w_m wide at its foot, h_m high over the sill stone it sits on (0.5 m over the floor, where TombKit.rest_place sits it; the stone stands 0.62 m out into the room), depth_m deep. sconce: niche_cup as above; niche_d_m: the niche's depth into the wall; cup_m: the stone cup's size (wide, high, deep); the flame stands in the cup a little inside the niche, its light 0.32 m out in front of it (where the old bracket held the flame: the rooms lit as §EX.4 counts them). stairs: block_steps, each step one block of the stone, a share settled (a little sunk, a little turned; settle), over the ramp you walk. dressing: coffins, the heart's box, the fallen slab, rubble (fallen wall stones and slab pieces), the hearth's kerb (nine stones where the campfire's ring stood), the airways' carved surrounds and the vents' flues, all the style's stone.
_help.style_by_theme: Which style each crawler.json theme is built in. by_theme (the wall preset) stays as built and must agree with the style's walls.preset. A theme not listed takes default. Built 7 Oct (Claude Code): the tomb is andean_tomb; a style's walls.preset is the wall preset (by_theme agrees, and the checks say so). TombKit.style_of reads it too, for the tomb's module and heights (§EX.2, queue 46).
